capabilities: Highlight and annotate PDF and EPUB documents
Track and search annotations in a sidebar
Export annotations to a formatted Markdown file
Reorder annotations by date or document position
extras: Only one plugin can open EPUBs at a time; the README says to disable any other EPUB-opening plugin. Annotations are stored in sidecar JSON files next to the documents and open read-only if the file is unreadable. Not suited to comics or two-page-spread e-books.
intentEvidence: PDF++ has the most features of Obsidian readers, but is clunky for some workflows, and doesn't work with EPUBs.
motivation: The author wanted to highlight and annotate PDFs and EPUBs and keep the resulting notes entirely inside Obsidian, replacing Zotero and separate EPUB readers.
problem: Obsidian's own PDF viewer has no annotation tools and does not open EPUBs, so readers turn to Zotero or external reader apps.

relations.evidence: PDF++ has the most features of Obsidian readers, but is clunky for some workflows
Zotero might be the best annotation app, but you might want to keep everything in Obsidian.

summary: PDF and EPUB reader that adds highlighting and notes with a sidebar annotation tracker and one-click Markdown export.
